nodes.abstract: This paper presents an extensive bibliometric analysis examining the integration of soft robotics within modern minimally invasive surgical procedures for the period 2021-2026.The research objective is to evaluate the technological transition from conventional rigid instruments to adaptable, bio-inspired systems designed for restricted anatomical navigation.The methodology employs a systematic scientometric approach, utilizing the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) workflow to analyze high-impact publications from primary scientific databases.By mapping global expertise and the evolution of key terminologies, the study identifies critical points of convergence between diverse technical solutions.The results demonstrate a significant shift toward multimodal locomotion and advanced haptic feedback interfaces, revealing a 20% increase in publications focused on autonomous control of deformable structures.Furthermore, the inclusion of early 2026 data highlights emerging trajectories in taskoptimized sensor selection.These findings provide a structured framework for identifying research gaps and aligning future developments with current clinical requirements in robot-assisted surgery.

AI-Driven Intrusion Detection in Industrial IoT: A Critical Survey of Computational Intelligence Approaches
nodes.abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) revolutionizes industrial operations by integrating smart sensors, advanced analytics, and machine learning to optimize manufacturing and supply chain processes. However, the rapid growth of IIoT presents tremendous cybersecurity challenges, as the increasing number of connected devices makes these systems more susceptible to cyberattacks. Intrusion detection systems (IDS) are vital for monitoring network and system activity to prevent and identify malicious attacks in IIoT. This paper discusses the role of AI- and computational-intelligence-driven IDS in protecting IIoT networks, addressing crucial challenges such as device heterogeneity, real-time operational limitations, and the mission-critical nature of industrial systems. Traditional IDS solutions are challenged by high false positives and dynamic cyber threats, and AI-based methods are a necessary evolution. Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) improve the effectiveness of IDS by enhancing anomaly detection, minimizing false alarms, and learning new attack patterns in dynamic IIoT environments. The paper discusses current IDS technologies, emphasizing their strengths and weaknesses in IIoT security. AI-based IDS utilizes deep learning, hybrid models, and feature engineering to improve accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, future directions in industrial cybersecurity include federated learning for decentralized security, lightweight AI models for resource-scarce IIoT devices, and blockchain for secure data exchange. AI-based IDS can protect critical infrastructure and provide reliable, safe, and resilient industrial processes in IIoT by addressing these issues. The present study highlights the growing role of AI and computational intelligence in making industrial cybersecurity resilient against evolving threats.

nodes.name: Utilidad de la imagen multimodal en el diagnóstico de un linfoma óseo primario del húmero proximal con baja avidez en PET/CT Value of multimodal imaging in the diagnosis of primary bone lymphoma of the proximal humerus with low PET/CT avidity
nodes.venue: Revista Colombiana de Hematología y Oncología
nodes.abstract: Introduction Primary bone lymphoma (PBL) is a rare extranodal malignancy that may mimic metastasis, myeloma, osteomyelitis, or sarcoma, making early diagnosis challenging. Clinical case A 60-year-old man presented with progressive right shoulder pain for three months. Radiography revealed an aggressive lytic lesion in the humeral head and proximal metaphysis. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated infiltrative marrow replacement, cortical permeation, soft-tissue extension, and ipsilateral axillary lymphadenopathy. 18F-FDG PET/CT showed moderate focal uptake (SUVmax 4.2) without distant disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed primary bone diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, non-germinal center subtype, with a high Ki-67 index. The case was staged as IIE and treated with six cycles of R-CHOP followed by consolidative radiotherapy, achieving complete metabolic response and remission at 18 months. Conclusion This case highlights the value of multimodal imaging and image-guided biopsy for timely diagnosis of PBL, even when PET/CT uptake is only moderate.

Urban Growth at the Edge of Limits: Assessing Land-System Change, Biosphere Integrity, and Freshwater Stress in Greater Accra through the Planetary Boundaries Framework
nodes.abstract: This study examines environmental transformation in Greater Accra between 2000 and 2020 through selected dimensions of the Planetary Boundaries framework, with attention to land-system change, biosphere integrity and freshwater stress. The analysis used Landsat 7 satellite imagery obtained from the United States Geological Survey, together with district shapefiles from the Ghana Open Data Initiative. A descriptive longitudinal design was adopted, and the imagery was processed in ArcMap and ENVI 5.1 using image pre-processing, gap filling, calibration, layer stacking, supervised classification, Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) analysis and post-classification change detection. The study was conceptually informed by the Environmental Kuznets Curve, Ecological Modernisation Theory and Planetary Boundaries Theory. Results indicate marked land-use and land-cover transformation over the two decades. Built-up land increased by 102.3%, while water bodies, grassland and dense forest declined by 77.7%, 87.3% and 75.7%, respectively. The reduction in vegetated surfaces suggests pressure on biosphere integrity, while the contraction of surface water bodies indicates growing freshwater-related stress. The combined pattern of urban expansion, vegetation loss and declining water coverage points to increasing pressure on selected planetary boundary dimensions within Greater Accra. The findings suggest that population growth, infrastructure development and land conversion are important drivers of ecological change in the region. By connecting observed land-cover dynamics to threshold-oriented sustainability thinking, the study offers context-specific evidence for urban environmental planning in a rapidly changing metropolitan region. It concludes that urban growth in Greater Accra requires stronger spatial planning, improved enforcement of land-use regulations and greater integration of green infrastructure and nature-based solutions to support development within ecological limits.

nodes.name: The Digital Methane Emissions Atlas: A Unified Geospatial Decision Framework for Multi-Source Methane Episode Fusion, Reconciliation, Prioritization, and Monitoring Design
nodes.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the Digital Methane Emissions Atlas, a confidentiality-safe geospatial decision framework that converts heterogeneous methane observations into defensible operational decisions. Methane mitigation in oil and gas now depends less on isolated detection and more on integrating evidence into a single auditable workflow. The Atlas addresses this need through an episode-centric analytical chain spanning fusion, reconciliation, evidence assessment, prioritization, lifecycle tracking, hotspot intelligence, benchmarking, and monitoring design. Using a synthetic but structurally realistic Kazakhstan portfolio, the framework consolidates satellite, aerial, drone, LDAR, and fixed-sensor detections into fused methane episodes with preserved source lineage; reconciles event-level rates through a precision-weighted posterior; and converts observational heterogeneity into interpretable evidence consistency and decision readiness scores. Operational extensions estimate breach-oriented risk, expected abatement, intervention utility, recurrence-oriented follow-up needs, and closure likelihood. Representative outputs trace a high-priority episode from multi-source detection through posterior reconciliation, lifecycle interpretation, field benchmarking, and staged monitoring expansion under budget constraints. The contribution is a unified, methodology-first architecture rather than a single predictive model. The current implementation remains a synthetic, pre-linked, heuristic prototype rather than a fully calibrated industrial MRV platform, but it demonstrates a credible foundation for multi-scale methane decision support at event, field, and portfolio levels.

nodes.name: Square-Lattice Moiré Sensing and Chirality Switching in an Intraocular Lens: A Multimodal Optical Platform for Sensitive Detection via Liquid-Crystal-like Birefringence
nodes.abstract: We report Moiré fringe formation, subsatellite diffraction, and spontaneous chirality switching in a commercial intraocular lens (IOL) illuminated through a square lattice aperture driven by a serpentine-channel motor. Application of an external static magnetic field breaks the mutual exclusivity of the Rocket and Moiré modes, enabling dual-mode coexistence analogous to coupled-mode phenomena reported for two-layer optical cavities. Sequential introduction of DC current and acoustic vibration (tuning fork) progressively sharpens fringe contrast and expands the Rocket mode radius. Under sustained identical conditions, the Moiré rotational sense spontaneously reverses—a stochastic chirality switching consistent with two nearly degenerate chiral ground states. FFT analysis of region-of-interest (ROI) brightness time series reveals that DC current induces splitting of the dominant spectral peak (Δf ≈ 0.55 Hz, center ROI; Δf ≈ 0.75 Hz, ring ROI), a Rabi-splitting-like mode bifurcation not present in the unperturbed baseline. These results establish two complementary sensing modalities: IOLs (liquid-crystal-like birefringent optics) with square-lattice excitation provide high sensitivity to subtle refractive and polarization changes, while honeycomb-mode convex-lens systems reveal fundamental structural transitions. The platform is reproducible with consumer-grade optics and is applicable to label-free optical sensing, topological photonics, and IOL quality assessment

nodes.name: Spatio-temporal considerations enhance forest fire prediction in Fujian Province
nodes.abstract: Abstract The intensification of global climate change has led to more frequent forest fires, making accurate prediction of fire occurrences critical for prevention and mitigation. This study utilizes forest fire occurrence data in Fujian Province from 2012 to 2020, combined with meteorological, vegetation, and topographic factors, to construct predictive models aimed at exploring the spatial and spatio-temporal characteristics of fire-driving factors. We compared the performance of the global Random Forest (RF), Geographically Weighted Random Forest (GWRF), and Spatio-Temporal Weighted Random Forest (STWRF) models. The results demonstrate that the STWRF model achieved the best performance, with superior fitting results and higher predictive accuracy. Elevation was identified as a key factor influencing forest fire occurrence in Fujian Province, where fires are most frequent from December to April in the central and northern regions, shifting to the central and southern regions during May to November. By incorporating spatio-temporal weights, the STWRF model enhances predictive performance and provides a solid theoretical foundation for policymakers to implement targeted forest fire prevention measures in response to spatio-temporal variations.

nodes.name: Scale-dependent effects of forest spatial structure on gross primary productivity across China
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
nodes.abstract: Forest spatial structure is a key dimension of ecosystem change, yet its scale-dependent relationships with gross primary productivity (GPP) remain insufficiently understood at large spatial extents. Using multi-source remote sensing datasets and national forest information for China from 2000 to 2020, we quantified how forest-cover spatial heterogeneity and forest structural variability were associated with GPP across multiple spatial scales. Local variance (LV), local standard deviation (LSD), and local coefficient of variation (LCV) were derived from forest cover (FC) using moving-window analysis to characterize forest spatial structure. Generalized additive models (GAMs) were employed to assess scale-dependent explanatory power, and Getis–Ord Gi* statistics were used to identify hotspot and coldspot regions of spatial-structure-induced productivity changes. Results show a clear scale-dependent pattern, with model explanatory power decreasing monotonically as spatial scale increases, indicating that forest spatial-structure effects are more evident at finer scales. Variable importance analysis reveals that forest spatial-structure metrics dominate at fine scales but decline with increasing scale. Spatially, the estimated effects of forest spatial structure on GPP displayed pronounced heterogeneity and clustering across China. Hotspot–coldspot analysis and sensitivity zoning revealed regionally aggregated patterns of positive, negative, and weak responses, indicating that forest spatial-structure effects are spatially organized and regionally dependent. The sensitivity classification further demonstrated that integrating effect magnitude, spatial clustering intensity, and temporal change provides an effective framework for identifying response types and high-sensitivity regions. Overall, this study highlights that the relationship between forest spatial structure and ecosystem productivity is neither scale-invariant nor spatially uniform, but instead characterized by strong scale dependence and regional differentiation. These findings provide large-scale empirical evidence for understanding structure–function relationships in forest ecosystems and offer basis for region-specific forest management and ecological restoration under global change.

Sat2City v2: Native 3D City Asset Generation from a Single Satellite Image
nodes.abstract: Generating explicit 3D city assets from a single satellite image is important for digital twins, urban simulation, and geospatial intelligence. Unlike satellite-to-street-view synthesis, the task requires a reusable textured mesh with plausible geometry and controllable appearance rather than a 3D proxy optimized only for rendering a small set of images or videos. The ICCV Sat2City framework made a first step by conditioning cascaded sparse-voxel latent diffusion on satellite-derived height maps, but its appearance was random, its training data were synthetic, and its task-specific VAE did not scale well to noisy real-world reconstructions. We present Sat2City v2, a journal extension that adapts a pretrained native structured-latent 3D foundation model to weakly aligned satellite images and textured meshes. We build a real-world dataset with 16,241 satellite-mesh pairs across 24 regions in 9 cities. Instead of learning a 3D representation from noisy city meshes, Sat2City v2 encodes each mesh into a pretrained native 3D latent space, fine-tunes a satellite-conditioned geometry flow, and uses the decoded shape to anchor satellite-conditioned texturing. This retains Sat2City's geometry-to-appearance cascade while enabling appearance-controllable generation from the satellite input. Experiments on metric-scale DSM reconstruction and generative city-asset benchmarks for geometry and appearance show that Sat2City v2 achieves the best overall performance among evaluated baselines. Overall, Sat2City v2 advances satellite-to-city generation from rendering-oriented 3D proxies to explicit textured mesh assets, supported by, to the best of our knowledge, the first documented satellite-mesh paired dataset collected from matched geographic crops for this asset-level task. Project page: https://ai4city-hkust.github.io/Sat2City-v2/

nodes.name: SRFNet: end-to-end deep learning for multi-angle SAR image registration and fusion
nodes.abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images hold significant potential for various applications. However, a single-view SAR image provides limited scene information. Multi-angle imaging has become a key means to acquire complete scene information. However, multi-angle SAR images commonly exhibit complex geometric distortions among them, such as translational, rotational, and distortion. Traditional registration and fusion methods usually perform registration and fusion in separate steps, which often leads to error accumulation, resulting in reduced fusion quality and affecting the performance of subsequent tasks such as target recognition. Therefore, we propose an end-to-end deep-learning-based method for multi-angle SAR image registration and fusion (SRFNet). This method integrates image registration and image fusion into a unified end-to-end network for joint optimization. We design a multi-scale feature-based flow prediction network that performs image registration in a phased manner: first by executing affine registration, followed by deformable registration through a coarse-to-fine strategy. Furthermore, a multi-scale spatial attention module is incorporated into the fusion network to achieve adaptive integration among images. Experimental results on two public datasets demonstrate that SRFNet achieves superior performance in both image registration and fusion tasks compared with existing state-of-the-art methods. By effectively integrating the registration and fusion processes, our approach exhibits consistent and advanced performance across diverse evaluation metrics and datasets, thereby providing a more reliable information foundation for downstream tasks such as target recognition.
